articles.headline: Kylian Mbappé refuses to criticise referee despite Madrid derby 'mistakes'
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé has refused to criticise the referee in charge of Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, despite admitting that official Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias made "mistakes" in his handling of the match.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappé has refused to criticise the referee in charge of Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, despite admitting that official Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias made "mistakes" in his handling of the match.

Madrid coach José Mourinho claimed on Sunday that Ortiz Arias had failed to show "two clear red cards" for rough, first-half challenges by Kang-in Lee and Cristian Romero, bringing a printout with photos of the incidents into his post-game news conference.

The result left Madrid six points behind LaLiga leaders Barcelona with just seven games played going into the international break -- with a Clásico to come at Camp Nou in October -- leaving Mourinho under pressure already in his second spell at the Bernabéu.

"I don't think I've ever been a player who talks much about referees," Mbappé told Diario AS in an interview in Switzerland, where he has agreed a new sponsorship deal with the brand On.

"I'm not going to start now. I have my own thoughts, but I'll keep them to myself... Referees are human, they make mistakes -- and those were mistakes -- but I don't want to get into that."

Romero was shown a yellow card for treading on Jude Bellingham's knee -- after a VAR check, when Bellingham had initially been cautioned for the clash -- while Lee escaped punishment for a high boot on Federico Valverde's ankle.

Atlético then went ahead in the second half at the Metropolitano through Alejandro Grimaldo's penalty after Dean Huijsen had been sent off, before Jonathan David made it 2-0, and then Antonio Rüdiger pulled a late goal back for Madrid.

It's a second defeat for Mourinho's side this season, after losing 1-0 at Real Betis earlier this month.

"[It's] a step backwards," Mbappé said, when asked about the derby loss. "It's very tough, we wanted to win, and we knew what kind of game it would be.

"But the team gave everything, and we're moving forward, because there's still a long way to go this season, and we have to stay on the right track... We have to work, and do more. We have to put the work in."

Mbappé will now join up for international duty with France under new coach Zinedine Zidane, who was one of the forward's childhood idols.

Zidane -- who has replaced long-term boss Didier Deschamps -- was working behind-the-scenes at Madrid when Mbappé first went on trial to the Spanish capital as a youngster.

- José Mourinho blasts ref, VAR: 'Two clear red cards' for Atlético Madrid

- Jonathan David winner helps Atlético Madrid down Real Madrid

- Barcelona's Andreas Christensen injures thigh, doubt for next Clásico

"It's a new era with a new coach," Mbappé said. "The Nations League is coming up, with four matches to see how things go, and it'll be a new experience for everyone, because we've only ever known Deschamps. It'll be a change for us, but I think everything will go really well.

"[Zidane] was the first person to pick me up and take me to Real Madrid, to the training complex, when I was 13 or 14, it was a long time ago.

articles.descriptionJa: キーオンテ・ジョージとジャズの延長契約をはじめ、主要なフリーエージェント契約や延長契約を評価します。
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Sept. 21: Thompson gets five-year extension from Pistons

Ausar Thompson terms: Five years, $155 million

Grade: B-

It's fitting that Thompson agreed to his rookie extension within a few hours of Keyonte George doing the same, because both players signed for nearly identical amounts even though they have polar opposite playing styles.

While George, who inked a five-year, $157.5 million extension with the Jazz, is a budding offensive star who might be the worst defensive player in the league, Thompson is an offensive liability who might be the NBA's best perimeter defender.

Thompson finished third in Defensive Player of the Year voting last season, behind only Victor Wembanyama and Chet Holmgren, as he led the league in steals and routinely locked up the opponents' top scorer. Largely because of his spectacular defensive prowess, the Pistons have been better with Thompson on the floor in every season of his career to date.

The concerns about his future come on the other end, because his shooting form, which was never strong to begin with, has gone backward. Last season, Thompson made just seven total 3-pointers on 23% accuracy, counting both regular season and playoffs.

Compared to his brother, Amen, who signed a five-year, $208 million extension earlier this offseason, Ausar has demonstrated less offensive potential. Amen isn't a 3-point marksman, either, but he at least improved to 78% at the free-throw line last season, suggesting untapped shooting potential, while Ausar made just 57% of his free throws. Amen has also been better than his brother at scoring on drives and handling the ball; there's a reason he averaged 18.3 PPG last season to Ausar's mere 9.9.

That's not to say Ausar is completely unproductive; he's effective in transition and a solid offensive rebounder -- a must, given how often he hangs out near the basket -- and the Pistons have still been better with him on the court than off, even on the offensive end.

articles.headline: Carrick has an impossible job at Man United after transfer failures
articles.description: Manchester United's players aren't good enough and the club isn't doing enough to rectify that, so where does that leave manager Michael Carrick?
articles.headlineJa: 補強失敗のマンUで、キャリック監督は困難を極める難題に直面
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの選手層は不十分であり、クラブもそれを是正するための十分な手立てを講じていない。マイケル・キャリック監督はどのような立場に置かれているのか？
articles.body:
Michael Carrick is failing at Manchester United because his bosses have handed him an impossible job.

A two-year contract as head coach, with the option of a 12-month extension, was Carrick's reward this summer for salvaging United's season from the wreckage of Ruben Amorim's woeful 14-month reign and delivering qualification for the UEFA Champions League. But having given Carrick the job he always wanted, United then told him he would have to do it with one arm tied behind his back after they missed out on each of his top transfer targets and left significant holes in his squad unfilled.

Welcome to reality of the modern Manchester United -- the club that has made mistakes for so long under the ownership of the Glazer family and minority shareholder Jim Ratcliffe that the team is now the equivalent of a house with a leaking roof, broken plumbing and damp on the walls, with nothing but a paint brush to make everything look better.

Carrick, a midfielder who won every major honor at least once during a 12-year playing career at Old Trafford, enjoyed the good days under Sir Alex Ferguson and witnessed the start of the slide under David Moyes, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho. But even though the 45-year-old has experienced the rough with the smooth, it is clear that he has inherited a bigger mess than any of his predecessors.

Sunday's 1-1 draw at Fulham, earned by an 89th minute equalizer scored by Matheus Cunha, ensured that United head into the international break with five points from five games -- their joint-worst start to a Premier League season. And the pressure is building on Carrick.

With less than three years of managerial experience on his CV following a stint in the EFL Championship with Middlesbrough, Carrick is underqualified for a role as demanding and difficult as the United job, but he earned the right to take it on permanently by guiding the team to a third-place finish last season.

However, after being so badly let down by the club's transfer dealings during the summer -- Carrick himself has diplomatically stuck to the club line of seeking value and financial sense in the market -- he has been left with a squad that is not equipped to succeed and will also fail under whoever replaces him if he ends up losing his job soon.

With Casemiro leaving for Inter Miami as a free agent and Manuel Ugarte -- now injured -- deemed not good enough for United, Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes were Carrick's top two targets to rebuild his midfield this summer. But Anderson left Nottingham Forest for Manchester City in a £116 million move and Fernandes opted to leave West Ham for Tottenham rather than United for £85 million.

United also considered Newcastle midfielders Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães, but quickly ruled out a move for the pair, who joined Spurs (£92.5 million) and Arsenal (£75 million) respectively, due to the fees involved.

articles.headline: Week 2 impact on the NFC: Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels hurt
articles.description: Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels both got injured. The Packers nearly lost to the Jets. The Saints upset the Ravens. And three teams have a claim as the NFC's best.
articles.body:
It's hard to say that any week of an NFL season can feel seismic, especially when it's the second week of the campaign. But I believe we're going to look back on Week 2 and say it was extraordinarily impactful in deciding and decoding the NFC.

Injuries to young quarterbacks were the biggest stories of the day, but we also saw several of the conference's top contenders reaffirm themselves with big victories, a couple of teams we're still not sure about squeak by and a preseason contender narrowly save itself from the 0-2 cliff. We even saw the NFC South get on the board with a pair of victories.

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

Let's run through some of the results and events from Sunday that might really matter in the NFC's big picture and break down how they played out and how they impact the conference moving forward. I'll start in Dallas, where the Commanders are facing serious short- and long-term questions about what's next.

Jump to:

WSH and Daniels' injury

CHI and Williams' injury

NO and its big win

GB and its near loss

Three teams at the top

Washington Commanders (0-2)

Lost 37-20 to the Cowboys

Sunday showed why organizations were both transfixed and terrified by the idea of drafting Jayden Daniels as their quarterback of the future. For most of the first half, Daniels was singlehandedly propelling the Commanders forward on offense. In addition to going 11-of-17 for 96 yards as a passer, he picked up five first downs with his legs, scrambling seven times for 69 yards. Having a QB capable of bailing the offense out and picking up explosive plays in the process gives the Commanders a floor that most other teams don't have on a weekly basis.

And then, on the final play of the first half, we saw the other side of the coin. With the Commanders passing up a field goal attempt to try to score a touchdown with three seconds remaining, Daniels took the snap from under center and got caught up in the footwork of left guard Chris Paul. As Daniels fell to the ground, he tried to brace with his left elbow, only for it to visibly give way and dislocate. He somehow got up and threw an incomplete pass and then did not return after halftime in a game that got away from Washington after the break.

The injury is likely to sideline Daniels for an extended period. He missed four games after dislocating the same elbow in Week 9 a year ago, then reaggravated the injury in Week 14 and did not return over the remainder of the season. Missing a month would be a season-altering injury for the Commanders, who are already 0-2 and about to face the defending champion Seahawks in their home opener next week. Marcus Mariota is a capable backup, but the veteran doesn't offer the same sort of explosiveness and calmness under pressure that Daniels exhibited during his remarkable rookie season.

articles.headline: 2026 MLB awards tracker: Odds for MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year
articles.description: Who are the favorites to win seasonlong honors? Here are the odds for MVP, Cy Young and Rookie of the Year in the AL and NL.
articles.body:
As the season winds down its final week of play, Pete Crow-Armstrong is running away with the National League MVP award, to the point where no action is being taken any longer, with Shohei Ohtani on the IL. Yordan Alvarez has also seemingly locked up the American League MVP honor with -6000 odds, with Junior Caminero the only close challenger at 13-1.

The AL Cy Young race is also all but done from a betting perspective, with no lines being currently listed. Cam Schlittler seems to be a near-lock to claim the trophy, with only Dylan Cease in the ever-quieting conversation. On the NL side, Jacob Misiorowski looks to be well on his way to winning his first Cy Young award, showing -8000 odds to Chris Sale's 20-1.

Meanwhile, the NL Rookie of the Year race is also no longer showing lines, with RBI-machine Sal Stewart as the clear top choice. In the AL, Kevin McGonigle is the solid favorite at -3500, with Parker Messick coming in at a distant 13-1.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  at time of publication. You can also find the latest odds for each team to win the World Series here.

articles.headline: Antoine Semenyo happy to lead Man City's attack if needed
articles.description: Antoine Semenyo is ready to take on the challenge of leading Manchester City's attack if needed.
articles.body:
Antoine Semenyo is ready to take on the challenge of leading Manchester City's attack if needed.

The Ghana international underlined his finishing ability with two clinical strikes in City's thrilling 5-3 victory over Sunderland in the Premier League on Sunday.

The prolific output of Erling Haaland, who was also on target as Enzo Maresca's side maintained their 100% start to the campaign, means City are rarely short of goals.

But the club's summer transfer activity has left them with no clear replacement for Haaland should the Norwegian miss any games.

Maresca has identified winger Semenyo as the most obvious alternative and the 26-year-old would be happy to step up.

Semenyo said: "I've heard about his backup striker thing. I don't know where it's come from!

"But, yes, if I need to, then I'll do it. I've no problem in doing that."

Of his finishing, he added: "I think that just comes naturally.

"Once I'm in front of the goal, I know it doesn't move. So as long as I hit it in the corner, hit it with a good connection, I know it will go in."

City were pushed all the way by Sunderland, who showed no sign of weariness from their midweek Europa League outing.

Brian Brobbey scored a hat trick for the visitors but Semenyo's double and Haaland's late effort completed the job for City, for whom Enzo Fernández and Rayan Cherki also struck.

Both sides had numerous other chances in a frantic game. Haaland missed an open goal for City while Brobbey hit the bar and Rúben Dias had to clear off the line. Sunderland also felt they should have had a penalty for handball against Elliot Anderson.

Semenyo said: "It was a tough one. Physically, we knew it would be like that -- duels, aerial balls, set-pieces.

"We knew it would be a fight, and we just needed to stick together collectively and win our individual duels and get three points, which we've done.

"Sometimes it is going to be like that, not every game you can control. You just have to ride the waves. We knew if we got our chances, we would score."

- Erling Haaland sets unique goal milestone as Man City beat Sunderland

- Enzo Maresca relieved as Manchester City pass difficult Sunderland test

City have now won seven games in succession in all competitions since their defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield.

With a three-point lead at the top of the Premier League, it has been a strong start under new manager Maresca but Semenyo feels there is still room for improvement yet.

He said: "Everyone feels good. It's where we want to be, but we're not going to get too complacent, too relaxed. We know that there's a lot more games to go.

"We just want to continue winning, we just have to keep going.

"It's seven or eight weeks we've been together now, so it's not been too long, but we're doing well. We're winning our games and we'll keep improving."

articles.headline: Every team's odds to win the World Series: Dodgers remain favorites as playoffs loom
articles.description: Every MLB team's odds to win the 2026 World Series, led by the Dodgers. Milwaukee and Tampa Bay continue to see odds improvement.
articles.body:
After multiple months of having the best record in Major League Baseball, the Milwaukee Brewers remain the second-favorite to win the 2026 World Series, shortening to +600 from +650 week-over-week. The New York Yankees, previously in that slot are tied for third-best with the AL-leading Tampa Bay Rays at +850.

The Los Angeles Dodgers are still the World Series favorites -- as they have been for the entire season -- but their current +195 is slightly longer than the +170 they showed just one month ago. The Boston Red Sox and Atlanta Braves (both 14-1) round out the top six.

Meanwhile, the Chicago White Sox (close to locking down at least a wild-card spot) sit at 25-1. Chicago was an astonishing 400-1 before the season and is one of the largest liabilities in a variety of futures markets across the sportsbook marketplace.

Odds by DraftKings Sportsbook  at time of publication.
